item.title: Tennessee State Trooper Behind 'Cassius Thundercock' Meme IDed Online, And His Chin Is Real
item.description: The clip of the police officer resurfaced on TikTok in August 2025 and went viral that November, inspiring the nickname "Cassius Thundercock" and memes in which people dress up as him and jokingly portray him as a cartoonishly crooked, aggressive cop who always turns his bodycam off to deal with people who wrong him. One of the most common jokes is that Cassius has had his bodycam turned off since Vietnam, meaning the Vietnam war.

item.title: The Earliest Example Of 'The Council Will Decide Your Fate' Meme Appeared Seven Years Ago Today
item.description: The Council Will Decide Your Fate is an image macro of a group of five people standing in a row with traffic cones over their heads. The picture often represents a group of decision makers due to their posture and headgear.

item.title: On This Day 13 Years Ago, The 'Mac And Charlie Notice Each Other' Meme Appeared In 'Always Sunny'
item.description: Mac and Charlie Notice Each Other refers to a memorable scene from the episode "The Gang Dines Out" of the It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia TV series in which characters Mac and Charlie stare at each other across a restaurant. Online, the scene has been used as an exploitable and an object labeling format, as well as has been referenced in jokes.

item.title: Abigail Lutz: The Viral LSU Gymnast Claiming To Be Livvy Dunne's Sister Explained
item.description: Abigail Lutz just went viral after allegedly flashing fans at an LSU game, all while doubling down on her claim that she's Livvy Dunne's sister. The internet isn't so convinced. item.title: Two Years Ago, The Glasses Loopy Plushie Took Over Social Media
item.description: Glasses Loopy Plushie refers to a plushie doll of the children's show character Loopy from Pororo wearing a wig and glasses. The doll inspired fan art and cosplaying, often to highlight characteristics of young Chinese women in Asia.
